To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the disclosure of intangible attributes is a key mechanism for firms to signal their corporate reputation to stakeholders and that the existence of governance mechanisms is a prerequisite for the disclosure of intangibles and the development of corporate reputation.

(i) the presence of financial expertise in the audit committee is an important determinant of the development and maintenance corporate reputation; (ii) the level of voluntary intangible assets disclosure is a significant determinant of corporate reputation; (iii) the presence of a non-executive chairman is a significant determinant in developing corporate reputation; (iv) the level of directors’ remuneration and directors’ share ownership are significant determinants of corporate reputations.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the role that corporate governance and intangible asset disclosure plays in the development and maintenance, or otherwise, of corporate reputation and the extent to which corporate reputation is influenced by financial performance and growth, directors’ share ownership, executive remuneration, financial expertise and financial gearing.
the role of corporate governance and voluntary disclosure in explaining the variation of corporate reputations as determined by stakeholders.
the development and maintenance, or the lack of, corporate reputation.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
corporate reputation is a result of the interaction of the corporate governance mechanisms and intangible assets disclosure.

the existence of corporate governance structures, the presence of financial expertise and lower levels of voluntary disclosure of intangibles are important in building and developing corporate reputations whereas the presence of financial gearing is important in maintaining corporate reputations once they are attained.

corporate governance structures and mechanisms are important in the development and maintenance process of corporate reputation, and that intangible resources are important to the development of reputation but not so much in the maintenance of corporate reputation.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

corporate governance mechanisms and disclosure of intangibles are significant in explaining the variation of corporate reputation as perceived by stakeholders and that the resource based view and signalling theory are useful in understanding the relationship between corporate governance and reputation.
corporate governance and the voluntary disclosure index are significant determinants of corporate reputations.

corporate governance mechanisms and intangibles disclosure are both important determinants of corporate reputations and that firms may choose to build and develop or maintain corporate reputation depending on their strategy and the market environment in which they operate.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the presence of corporate governance structures is a necessary but not sufficient condition for the development of a firm’s corporate reputation.
the disclosure of corporate reputation is not necessarily associated with the disclosure of intangible resources.

corporate governance structures are important in explaining corporate reputation, and the presence of corporate governance mechanisms may allow firms to draw on the benefits of intangible assets in the market place.
